arxiv-2306-05573.title: Microscopic intervention yields abrupt transition in interdependent magnetic networks
arxiv-2306-05573.creator: Bnaya Gross, Ivan Bonamassa, Shlomo Havlin
arxiv-2306-05573.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Bnaya Gross, Ivan Bonamassa, Shlomo Havlin. The study of interdependent networks has recently experienced a boost with the development of experimentally testable materials that physically realize their critical behaviors, calling for systematic studies that go beyond the percolation paradigm. Here we study the critical phase transition of interdependent spatial magnetic networks model where dependency couplings between networks are realized by a thermal interaction having a tunable spatial range.

arxiv-2307-04131.title: Carbon-Efficient Neural Architecture Search Conference: 2nd Workshop on Sustainable Computer Systems; July 9, 2023; Boston, MA, USA 2nd Workshop on Sustainable Computer Systems (HotCarbon ’23), July 9, 2023, Boston, MA, USA Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3604930.3605708 ISBN: 979-8-4007-0242-6/23/07 CCS:
arxiv-2307-04131.creator: Yiyang Zhao, Tian Guo
arxiv-2307-04131.description: Abstract . This work presents a novel approach to neural architecture search (NAS) that aims to reduce energy costs and increase carbon efficiency during the model design process. The proposed framework, called carbon-efficient NAS ( CE-NAS ), consists of NAS evaluation algorithms with different energy requirements, a multi-objective optimizer, and a heuristic GPU allocation strategy.

arxiv-2506-10160.title: Hybrid discrimination strategy based on photon-number-resolving detectors and mesoscopic twin-beam states
arxiv-2506-10160.creator: Luca Razzoli, Alex Pozzoli, Alessia Allevi
arxiv-2506-10160.description: Abstract State discrimination is a key challenge in the implementation of quantum communication protocols. Most optical communication protocols rely on either coherent states of light or fragile single-photon states, making it often difficult to achieve robustness and security simultaneously. In this work, we propose a hybrid strategy that operates in the mesoscopic intensity regime, leveraging robust quantum states of light.

arxiv-2510-00098.title: Dark forces suppress structure growth
arxiv-2510-00098.creator: Marco Costa, Cyril Creque-Sarbinowski, Olivier Simon, Zachary J. Weiner
arxiv-2510-00098.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Marco Costa, Cyril Creque-Sarbinowski, Olivier Simon, Zachary J. Weiner. No experimental test precludes the possibility that the dark matter experiences forces beyond general relativity—in fact, a variety of cosmic microwave background observations suggest greater late-time structure than predicted in the standard Λ \Lambda cold dark matter model.

pmc-11716954.title: Cerebrovascular reactivity as a candidate biomarker in small vessel disease related VCID
pmc-11716954.creator: Hanzhang Lu
pmc-11716954.description: BackgroundThe brain’s ability to perform a cognitive task is a dynamic process and requires small blood vessels to dilate or constrict in real time to adjust blood flow in a region‐specific manner. Cerebrovascular Reactivity (CVR) measures the ability of vessels to react to vasoactive challenges.

pmc-12505726.title: VIRI: a visualization tool for tree reconciliations
pmc-12505726.creator: Maurizio Patrignani, Giordano Dionisi, Blerina Sinaimeri, Tiziana Calamoneri
pmc-12505726.description: BackgroundCophylogeny reconciliation is a powerful method for analyzing host-symbiont coevolution. The cophylogeny problem consists of mapping the phylogenetic tree of the symbionts into the one of the hosts, including events such as duplications, co-speciation, host-switches, and extinctions by comparing the discrepancies between the topologies of the associated symbiont evolutionary trees.
